lesson.title: The Safe Second Serve Trap
lesson.hook: Your second serve lands in but gives the receiver room to attack.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you serve second, notice where and how the receiver meets it.

pro.label: Sinner and Alcaraz on second serves
pro.moment: On second serves Sinner aims mostly at the body: 44% on the deuce side, 63% on the ad side. Alcaraz goes to the body less (27% and 38%) and moves receivers with wide and T serves instead.
pro.read: Judge your second serve by the contact it gives back.

drill.name: Second serves only
drill.how: Play games where every point starts on a second serve. The server wins a bonus point when the return is struck above the receiver's shoulder or off the body.

steps.name: Two second serves, both in
steps.sit: Both second serves go in. Watch where the receiver meets each one.
steps.q: What's different about the two returns?
opts: They meet one further inside the court
They switch to the other wing
They have to run for the kick
steps.payoff: The safe serve reaches them chest high. The kick gets above their shoulder.
steps.principle: In is only half of it. What matters is where it lets them hit.
steps.why: Both are met on the backhand, near the baseline. The height is the difference: chest high invites an attack; above the shoulder makes it hard.
steps.take: Your second serve is in — now check the height it reaches them at.

lines.A: Both were met on the baseline — the height changed, not the depth.
lines.B: Both were backhands — the height changed, not the wing.
lines.C: Right — the safe one arrives chest high, the kick above their shoulder.
lines.D: Neither made them run — the kick simply climbed higher.

steps.name: Four second serves
steps.sit: Your safe second serve lets this receiver step in and attack.
steps.q: Which change stops them stepping in?
steps.payoff: Depth and kick take away the comfortable height.
steps.principle: Judge a second serve by the contact it gives the receiver.
steps.why: Shorter or slower still arrives chest high. More pace pushes them back but not up. Deep with kick climbs above the shoulder, and their return is weak.
steps.take: Second serve getting attacked? Add depth and kick, not just pace.

lines.A: Shorter, it sits up — they step in, and you're stretched.
lines.B: Deep with kick, it climbs above their shoulder — you're set early.
lines.C: More pace pushes them back, but it's still chest high — you're stretched.
lines.D: Slower, it sits up even more — they step in; you're stretched.

steps.name: A receiver who likes height
steps.sit: A different receiver handles high balls well. Watch how they deal with each serve.
steps.q: Which serve gives this receiver the most trouble?
opts: Slow and deep to the backhand
steps.payoff: For this receiver, width does what height did for the last one.
steps.principle: Serve to the receiver's problem, not your favourite serve.
steps.why: This receiver handles high balls, so the kick doesn't bother them. Out wide makes them reach, and a stretched return is weak.
steps.take: They like it high? Take them wide instead.

lines.A: They like it high — in balance, and they attack; you're stretched.
lines.B: Slow and deep to the backhand — in balance; you're stretched.
lines.C: Wide works too — they're reaching, and the return is weak.
lines.D: Low and wide, they reach on the run — a weak return; you're set.
